top_categories.workout_context: 89ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At White Rose Classic, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at White Rose Classic. Practice on hilly Dales roads, pro-peloton pedigree: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 125 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic White Rose Classic's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At mile 60 of 125, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
11,071ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of White Rose Classic. Train it until it feels boring.
11,071ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at White Rose Classic. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 11,071ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 125 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 11,071ft of climbing on hilly Dales roads, pro-peloton pedigree does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for White Rose Classic’s 125 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at White Rose Classic. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at White Rose Classic rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on hilly dales roads, pro-peloton pedigree to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and Road Specific to prepare you for 125 miles of hilly dales roads, pro-peloton pedigree in Ilkley, West Yorkshire, UK.
